newsitem.title: UK: UK Liberals likely to vote against budget tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: UK Liberals likely to vote against budget tax cuts.

text.p: Britain's minority Liberal Democrats are likely to vote against pre-election tax cuts which they expect in November's budget, treasury spokesman Malcolm Bruce said on Monday.
Bruce told the party's annual conference that its commitment to spend an extra two billion stg a year on education must come before its desire to get taxes down.

"Some people in the press tell us our position on income tax is risky. I say this -- there is no greater risk to this country's future than skimping on education for a penny off income tax," Bruce said.

Bruce said given the high level of public sector borrowing in the current financial year, "it's highly unlikely that we could change our position on income tax without retreating from our commitment to education."
"We will judge the budget on two issues this year -- does it provide the vital extra two billion stg investment in education? Is it consistent with responsible economic management?
"Because if it is not, be in no doubt we will vote against tax cuts," he added.
Bruce said he had challenged the opposition Labour Party to vote against tax cuts in last year's budget in order to conserve the money for education improvements, but they had abstained.
"Let me say this to (Labour leader) Tony Blair...You didn't have the guts to do that then. Will you have the guts to do it this year?," he said.
Bruce repeated his party's pledge to raise tax on incomes over 100,000 stg a year to 50 percent from the current 40 percent in order to relieve 750,000 low-paid people of income tax altogether.
He called for the Bank of England to be replaced by a UK reserve bank accountable to parliament but free from day-to-day political interference.
"This reform, together with a clear inflation target of nil to three percent, would avoid a return to boom-bust and guarantee low inflation and interest rates," he said.
